# Trove

> Trove is a free, open-source (GNU AGPL v3), self-hosted library server for ebooks, comics and audiobooks. It organises EPUB, PDF, MOBI, AZW3, FB2, CBZ/CBR/CB7 and M4B/M4A/MP3/Opus files, has a built-in web reader, fetches metadata automatically, supports multiple users, and syncs with Kobo e-readers, KOReader and OPDS reading apps. It is a maintained continuation of BookLore, and an alternative to Calibre-Web, Kavita and Komga.

Trove runs on your own Linux server, NAS or home lab, with Docker/Podman (image `ghcr.io/x2-consult/trove`), a Helm chart, or a native installer for Ubuntu and Debian (Java 25 and PostgreSQL). Nothing depends on a third-party service. Source code: https://github.com/X2-Consult/trove

Key features:

- Libraries on local disks or NAS shares (SMB/NFS), with safe writes to network storage
- Built-in reader for ebooks, comics, PDFs and audiobooks, with highlights, notes and reading progress
- Kobo sync (books, shelves and two-way reading progress), KOReader progress sync, OPDS catalogue, Komga-compatible API
- Automatic metadata from Google Books, Open Library, Amazon, Goodreads and more
- Custom shelves, rule-based Magic Shelves, series and author pages, full-text search
- Multiple users, per-user progress and shelves, library access and content restrictions, OIDC single sign-on
- BookDrop watched-folder import, Send to Kindle and email
- Moving from BookLore keeps libraries, users, reading progress and paired devices
